results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
This is a brew. No storm deck shows up in the current Premodern field. Only one Scourge storm card is both green and legal here: Hunting Pack. The others I checked are either illegal or off-color. Tendrils of Agony, Grapeshot and Mind's Desire are illegal in Premodern. Brain Freeze, Temporal Fissure and Wing Shards are legal but not green. So I built on the Elves shell and made Hunting Pack the finisher.

**What the field data says**
- Elves has 3 appearances in the field list, 0.6% of the meta. The card stats cover 7 Elves decks. One of them runs 2 Hunting Pack (14%). It has shown up in 31 lists across the format.
- Gabaman went 5-0 in a League on 10/11 with this core: Survival, Cradle, Priest, Quirion Ranger, Multani's Acolyte and Wirewood Symbiote.

**How the storm count builds**
- **Free and cheap spells:** Llanowar Elves, Fyndhorn Elves, Quirion Ranger and Wirewood Symbiote each cost one mana. Lotus Petal costs zero. Every cast adds to the storm count.
- **Replaying creatures:** Multani's Acolyte and Wirewood Symbiote return elves to your hand so you can cast them again for more storm.
- **Mana:** Gaea's Cradle (in 100% of Elves lists) and Priest of Titania (100%) produce the big mana for Hunting Pack. Hunting Pack is an instant, so you can also cast it at the end of the opponent's turn.
- **Payoff:** With storm at 6, one Hunting Pack makes seven 4/4s.
- **Wirewood Lodge:** It untaps a Priest or adds another use of an elf. It has not shown up in recent results.

**What I changed from stock Elves**
- I cut the red splash. That means no Anger, Squee or Mountain. Survival still finds Deranged Hermit, Yavimaya Granger and Masticore.
- I cut Tangle Wire (43% of lists). In its place are 4 Lotus Petal and 4 Hunting Pack.

**Sideboard**
- It follows the usual Elves board: Naturalize (100%), Tormod's Crypt (71%), Xantid Swarm and Uktabi Orangutan.
- Winter Orb (57% of Elves boards) works against your own mana. Only bring it in if you're the one doing the locking.

**Risks**
- Hunting Pack costs 7. A slow hand of mana creatures loses to Sligh (10.6% of the meta) and to sweepers.
- Tune it in Leagues before you take it to a Challenge.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
I built a Green-White (GW) Replenish deck for Premodern. It plays no blue. It passed the format check with no errors.

**Why green-white.** Every one of the 37 Replenish lists in the last 30 days plays blue. Attunement, Frantic Search, Intuition and Island are in all or nearly all of them. You can't get the stock list without blue. The closest real non-blue shell is Enchantress. It's tier A at 13.8% of the field, and 95 of its 96 lists run Replenish. So I took that shell and moved it toward the Replenish combo.

**Combo pieces.**
- 3 Replenish. Enchantress lists average 2.2. I went up one so you see it more often.
- 4 Parallax Wave and 3 Opalescence. Enchantress lists average 2.7 and 2.6. With Opalescence out, Parallax Wave turns into a creature and can exile itself.

**Getting enchantments into the graveyard.** Without blue you lose Attunement and Frantic Search. The deck fills the graveyard these ways instead:
- Seal of Cleansing (3) and Aura of Silence (1) sacrifice themselves.
- Solitary Confinement (2) makes you discard a card every upkeep.
- The rest comes from opponents removing your enchantments.

**Engine.** 4 Argothian Enchantress, 4 Enchantress's Presence, 4 Wild Growth, 3 Sterling Grove and 3 Mirri's Guile. Mirri's Guile is at 3, down from the usual 4, to make room for the extra combo copies.

**Lands.** Brushland, Serra's Sanctum, Windswept Heath, Wooded Foothills, Forest and Plains. No land in the deck makes blue mana.

**Sideboard.** This follows the usual Enchantress board. Xantid Swarm shows up in 97% of those boards, Tormod's Crypt in 98%, Aura of Silence in 82%, Sacred Ground in 81% and Gaea's Blessing in 72%.

**This is a brew.** The list is almost all stock Enchantress cards. But no recorded result runs 3 Replenish and 4 Parallax Wave in this shell, so treat it as untested. For a matchup-specific sideboard plan, name the opponent and I'll check the board against it.

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
I can't build this one as you asked. Tainted Pact is not legal in Modern.

- **Tainted Pact**: Odyssey instant. The lookup tool returns legalInFormat "illegal", and it has 0 Modern lists. Your server won't accept a list that includes it, and there's no legal card in Modern that does the same job.
- **Thassa's Oracle**: Legal in Modern. It shows up in 22 recent lists.

Without Pact, the combo doesn't work. In Legacy and Vintage, Pact exiles your whole library so Oracle wins on entry. Modern has no other way to exile your own library that I can confirm with the tools.

Oracle is not a main-deck card in the two Modern decks I checked:
- **Mono-Blue Belcher** (30 lists): wins with Goblin Charbelcher and Tameshi. Oracle is not in its main deck.
- **Necrodominance** (44 lists): mono-black midrange. Oracle is not played.

Here are some ways forward. Tell me which one you want:
1. **Find the 22 Oracle lists.** I'll check other strategies for Oracle, then build a list based on real results.
2. **A Modern Oracle brew.** Keep 4 Thassa's Oracle and add legal ways to empty your library or raise devotion to blue. This would be a brew, and I'd look up every card before adding it.
3. **Play Tainted Pact in a different format.** This tool only builds Modern decks, but Oracle plus Pact is a real combo in Legacy and Vintage.

results.prompt: I want a Modern Merfolk deck that can beat the current top decks.
results.text:
I built mono-blue Merfolk for Modern and it passed the legality check. It copies a real 5-0 Modern League list from Oct 13. The same player went 5-0 with nearly the same 75 on Oct 12. The only change between the two was 3 Subtlety in place of 3 Propaganda in the sideboard.

**Sample size.** Only 6 Merfolk lists showed up in the last 30 days. Both 5-0s came from that one player. I have no matchup win rates, so I can't promise this list beats the top decks. I can only show how the cards line up against them.

**The two top decks**
- Broodscale Combo is 17.3% of the field.
- Prowess is 9.3% of the field.

**Main deck**
- **Harbinger of the Seas** is in 6 of 6 lists. It turns nonbasic lands into Islands, and both top decks rely on nonbasics.
  - Broodscale plays about 16.7 nonbasics: Eldrazi Temple, Urza's Saga and Ugin's Labyrinth.
  - Prowess plays about 15.3: Steam Vents and fetchlands.
- **Aether Vial and Cavern of Souls** are each in 83% of lists. They get your creatures past counterspells.
- **Flare of Denial and Sink into Stupor** are each in 83% of lists. Snapback is in 50%. These give you free or cheap interaction.

**Sideboard**
I scored all four cards against both matchups. Every card hit.
- **4 Chalice of the Void.** Set it to 1 against Prowess, which plays about 4 Dragon's Rage Channeler and 3.8 Monastery Swiftspear. Set it to 2 against Broodscale to stop Basking Broodscale (4 copies) and Haywire Mite.
- **4 Consign to Memory.** It counters colorless spells, and Broodscale's Eldrazi are colorless: Basking Broodscale, Sowing Mycospawn, Emrakul and Devourer of Destiny. It is in 83% of Merfolk sideboards.
- **4 Force of Negation.** It counters noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. Use it against Prowess spells and combo pieces.
- **3 Propaganda.** Each attacker costs 2 mana. That slows the 1/1 and 1/2 Prowess creatures and also taxes an Emrakul attack.

**Option:** Use 3 Subtlety instead of Propaganda if you see more Broodscale than Prowess. It puts a creature spell back on top or bottom of the library, such as Devourer of Destiny or Sowing Mycospawn.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
I built a mono white control deck for Modern. It's a brew. Mono white control isn't in the current 30-day field, and the server tagged it Rogue with zero confidence. I started from the closest deck in the field, UW Control (2.2% of the meta, 44 league trophies), and kept its white cards.

**Cards taken from UW Control (84 decks):**
- **Solitude:** in 100% of lists, 3.9 copies on average. It's the core removal spell. You can cast it for free by exiling another white card from your hand, which is easy here because nearly every card is white.
- **Wrath of the Skies:** in 99%, 2.6 copies on average. It's a cheap board wipe that hits artifacts and enchantments too. That's good against Affinity and Broodscale Combo.
- **Orim's Chant and Isochron Scepter:** Orim's Chant is in 96% at 4 copies, Scepter is in 90%. Put Chant on Scepter and the opponent can't cast spells on your turn or theirs. That's the fun lock.
- **March of Otherworldly Light (81%) and Geier Reach Sanitarium (96%):** flexible removal and a land that lets you draw and discard.

**Cards I added for fun and power:**
- **Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Lyra Dawnbringer, Sunfall and Elspeth Conquers Death:** none of these have shown up in recent Modern results. They're the brew part, so expect them to be slow against the faster decks.
- **Archon of Emeria:** 18 decks across the format. It stops Storm and Prowess from casting more than one spell a turn.
- **Path to Exile (979 decks) and Portable Hole (225):** cheap removal. Urza's Saga can fetch Portable Hole from your deck.
- **Witch Enchanter and Emeria's Call:** each is a spell on one side and a land on the other. You get 25 land slots without flooding.

**Things to know:**
- **No Prismatic Ending:** it only scales with the number of colors you pay, so in mono white it only hits cards costing 1 or less. Portable Hole covers that job better.
- **No Day's Undoing:** UW Control plays it in 98% of lists, but it's a blue card.
- **Little card draw:** your extra cards come from Geier Reach and the two Elspeths.

**Sideboard:**
- **Faster decks:** High Noon (4,457 decks in the format) and Deafening Silence against Storm and Prowess. Kor Firewalker against red decks.
- **Graveyard decks:** Rest in Peace against Goryo's Vengeance and Living End.
- **Artifact decks:** Stony Silence against Affinity.

If you tell me which matchups you expect in leagues, I'll check each one and tune the sideboard for it.

results.prompt: Build a fast red aggro deck for Pauper.
results.text:
I built Mono-Red Rally. It's the fastest red aggro deck in Pauper right now. It's Tier B with a 2.8% meta share, 24 appearances and 32 League trophies in the last 30 days. Plain Mono-Red has only 2 appearances and no trophies, so I didn't use it. The list passed the legality check.

**How it wins:** You play cheap creatures early, then cast Goblin Bushwhacker or Rally at the Hornburg to make your team bigger and give it haste. Burn finishes the opponent. Almost every spell costs one mana. Only Burning-Tree Emissary, Rally and Reckless Impulse cost two, and Emissary pays its cost back when it enters. You can win on turn 3 or 4.

**Main deck choices, from 57 lists:**
- **In every list (100%):** 4 Burning-Tree Emissary, 4 Clockwork Percussionist, 4 Goblin Bushwhacker, 4 Goblin Tomb Raider, 4 Voldaren Epicure, 4 Lightning Bolt, 4 Galvanic Blast, 4 Rally at the Hornburg and 4 Great Furnace.
- **Mountains:** 14. The average list plays 13.8.
- **Reckless Impulse:** in 88% of lists. I play 4, as in the Challenge list I copied. The average is 3.
- **Experimental Synthesizer:** 3 copies, in 65% of lists. It's an artifact, which turns on Galvanic Blast's bonus damage (4 instead of 2). It also draws cards.
- **Chain Lightning:** 2 copies, in 61% of lists.
- **End the Festivities:** 1 copy, in 56% of lists. It kills a board of 1-toughness creatures.

The 60 matches NMT_Sco94's list, which went 3-0 in the Swiss rounds of a Pauper Challenge (2026-10-13), made top 8 and lost in the quarterfinals.

**Sideboard:** This is the field's usual sideboard for this deck. I haven't tuned it against any specific opponent.
- **Cast into the Fire (3):** in 98% of lists.
- **Red Elemental Blast (3) and Pyroblast (3):** in 74% and 67% of lists. Both answer blue decks like Faeries and Dimir Control.
- **Relic of Progenitus (3):** in 60% of lists. It shuts down graveyard decks.
- **End the Festivities (2 more):** in 82% of sideboards.
- **Smash to Smithereens (1):** in 58% of lists. Use it against Affinity.

**Faster option:** The 5-0 League list (JorGG, 2026-10-14) plays 4 Gingerbrute, 4 Wrenn's Resolve and 2 Inventor's Axe instead of Synthesizer, Impulse and Chain Lightning. It attacks harder but has less burn. Gingerbrute is in 30% of lists and Inventor's Axe in 39%.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
I built an Abzan Greasefang deck that fills its own graveyard. It's a brew. The server checked it and confirmed it's a legal Pioneer 60 with a 15-card sideboard.

**How it differs from the usual list**
- The stock Greasefang deck is Orzhov with Monument to Endurance, Fleeting Spirit, Iron-Shield Elf and Guardian of New Benalia. Monument shows up in 81% of 37 decks. Those cards are cut here.
- Instead, the deck mills itself to put vehicles in the graveyard:
  - 4 Stitcher's Supplier
  - 4 Satyr Wayfinder
  - 4 Grisly Salvage
  - 2 Cache Grab
- 2 Formidable Speaker can discard a vehicle and search for Greasefang in the same play.

**Vehicles**
- **4 Parhelion II:** The standard top end. Every one of the 37 lists plays it.
- **3 Thundering Broodwagon:** Greasefang brings it back each combat and returns it to hand at your end step. That means its enter trigger fires every turn and destroys an opponent's nonland permanent with mana value 4 or less. Cycling it for 2 also puts it straight into the graveyard. It shows up in 19% of Greasefang lists as a flex card.

**What's kept from the stock list**
- 4 Thoughtseize and 4 Fatal Push. Thoughtseize is in 100% of lists and Fatal Push in 81%.

**What's new or rare in results**
- **Satyr Wayfinder:** Has not shown up in any recent Pioneer results.
- **Grisly Salvage:** Appears in 3 lists across the whole format.
- **Stitcher's Supplier:** Fringe. Seen in 1 Greasefang-family list.
- None of the three has appeared in a list with Broodwagon, so this exact mix is untested.

**Mana**
25 lands for three colors. Overgrown Tomb, Llanowar Wastes, Brushland and Temple Garden cover green. Greasefang still needs white and black on turn 3, so Concealed Courtyard and Godless Shrine stay at 4 each.

**Sideboard**
This is based on the usual Greasefang sideboard, not a plan for a specific opponent:
- 3 Doorkeeper Thrull (81% of lists)
- 3 Pest Control (95%)
- 2 Soul-Guide Lantern (81%)
- 2 Duress
- 2 Bitter Triumph
- 2 Vanishing Verse
- 1 Esika's Chariot (a flex main-deck card in the Abzan version, used here as a sideboard option against removal-heavy decks)

**Risk**
Soul-Guide Lantern and other graveyard hate hit this version harder than the stock list. If your opponent removes the graveyard, Broodwagon is still a castable 6-drop. Parhelion II costs 8, so it's only realistic through Greasefang.

results.prompt: Give me a strong Golgari midrange list for Standard.
results.text:
I submitted the 60 and sideboard above, and the server says they're legal.

**First, the data is thin.** Golgari Midrange doesn't show up in the Standard tier list at all. Only 4 lists made results in the last 30 days. So I can't call this a top-tier deck, just the best Golgari result there is.

**Where the list comes from:** It's coffeee's Standard League 5-0 from 2026-09-22, card for card. The other two winning lists I pulled did badly: Marrchata went 1-3 in Challenge 16 on 2026-10-11, and DB_ruda went 0-2 in Challenge 16 on 2026-09-29. Both were slower decks built around planeswalkers. coffeee's is the only Golgari list with a winning record, so I built from it.

**How it plays:** It's a fast creature deck. Llanowar Elves (4) speed up your mana. Bejeweled Warg (4), Chief Warg's Company (4) and Head of the Hunt (2) are the wolves that do the attacking. Firdoch Core (3) and Unholy Annex (4) add more pressure. The cards most Golgari lists share:
- Requiting Hex: in 100% of the 4 lists, about 3.3 copies.
- Professor Dellian Fel: 100%, about 2.5 copies.
- Bitter Triumph: 75%.
- Shoot the Sheriff: 75%.
- Maelstrom Pulse: 75%.

**Lands:** There are 25 lands, but 4 Llanowar Elves give extra mana.

**Sideboard:** Mostly matches the usual Golgari board. Duress (4) is in 100% of the boards. Strategic Betrayal (2) is in 75%. Day of Black Sun and Intimidation Tactics are each in 50%. Ancient Vendetta, Deadly Cover-up and Heritage Reclamation aren't in other Golgari boards, but plenty of other Standard decks play them.

**A slower version:** If you'd rather play Golgari as a value deck than an aggro one, use the planeswalker shell instead. That means Vraska, the Cutting Glare (50% of lists, about 3.5 copies) and Garruk, Veiled Butcher (50%). Neither of those lists won a match in its Challenge, though.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
No Legacy deck can win on turn 1 every game. Every game starts with a random 7, so some hands just can't do it. Opponents also play Force of Will, Daze, and Thoughtseize. What I can give you is a fast combo deck that can win on turn 1 or 2 with a good hand and protects itself when it can't.

The list passed the legality check. It is HJ_Kaiser's 7-1 list that won Legacy Challenge 16 on 2026-10-04, copied card for card. It's the most all-in combo version of the two winning lists.

**Why Doomsday:**
- It's the best-performing fast combo deck in the current field: tier A, 5.7% meta share, 43 appearances, 37 league trophies.
- The Epic Storm (tier B, 3.6%) and Sneak and Show (tier B, 3.7%) can also win fast, but have fewer results.

**How it wins:**
1. Make mana with Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal, and Lion's Eye Diamond.
2. Cast Doomsday. It sets up a 5-card library.
3. Draw through that library, then cast Thassa's Oracle. You win when it enters with your library smaller than your blue devotion.

**Card choices:**
- **Core:** 4 Doomsday, 4 Dark Ritual, 4 Brainstorm, and 4 Force of Will are in 100% of 80 lists.
- **Lion's Eye Diamond:** in 99% of lists. It's the main source of explosive turn 1 mana.
- **Lotus Petal:** in 100% of lists, 2.7 copies on average. This list plays 3.
- **Street Wraith (4 here):** in 99% of lists. You can cycle it for free to draw into your Doomsday pile.
- **No Tamiyo:** Tamiyo is in 45% of lists. This version runs Personal Tutor (69%) and 3 Thoughtseize instead. That keeps it a pure combo deck.
- **Jace, Wielder of Mysteries (1):** in 33% of lists. It's a second way to win if Thassa's Oracle gets answered.

**Sideboard:** It follows the field's usual board. Barrowgoyf (66%), Dauthi Voidwalker (65%), Fatal Push (69%), Force of Negation (100%), and Murktide Regent (61%) let you board into a creature plan when opponents expect pure combo. This is a general board, not a plan for a specific opponent. Name an opponent and I'll build a sideboard plan for that matchup.

**What to expect:** Turn 1 wins only happen with the right hands. Most wins come on turn 2 or 3, after you've used discard and counterspells to clear the way.

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
**This is a brew.** You can't merge the two decks fully in Modern right now. The list above passed validation. It's a Living End deck with the Scam idea built in.

**What stops a full merge:**
- **Scam's main cards are banned.** Grief and Fury both come back as illegal in Modern.
- **There's no Scam data.** Scam has 0 decks in the last 30 days. It isn't on the strategy list, so there's no stock Scam list to start from.
- **Scam's 1-mana spells break cascade.** Undying Malice, Feign Death and Not Dead After All are legal but have 0 results. They cost 1 mana. Cascade casts the first nonland card that costs less than 3, so it would hit them instead of Living End. Persist costs 2 and has the same problem. I left all four out.

**How the merge works:**
- **Scam's plan is evoke a creature, then bring it back.** Here Living End does the bringing back. You evoke Subtlety, Endurance, Wistfulness or Solitude early. Living End returns them all at once and you get every enters trigger again.
- **The base is stock Living End.** It has 80 decks in the window. Shardless Agent is in 99%, Violent Outburst in 85%, Force of Negation in 100%. Endurance, Subtlety, Wistfulness and Generous Ent are all at 100%.
- **4 Solitude is the Scam piece.** It's legal and very common across Modern, but it hasn't shown up in any Living End list. It costs 5 mana, so it doesn't interfere with cascade. When Living End returns it, it exiles one of their creatures.
- **Solitude has a drawback.** Its evoke cost means exiling another white card from your hand. In the main deck the only other white cards are more copies of Solitude. After sideboarding, the 4 Clarion Conqueror are also white cards you can exile.
- **The 4 Solitude replace Curator and Riverwinder.** Those are the last nonland slots in stock lists, flex at 39% and 51%. Sacred Foundry (50%) and Temple Garden (65%) give you white mana to cast Solitude normally.

**Sideboard:** This is the average Living End sideboard. Mystical Dispute is in 100% of boards, Force of Vigor 93%, Inevitable Betrayal 78%, Clarion Conqueror 70%, Brotherhood's End 64%. Teferi is in 48% of boards, but only 5% of decks run him in the main.

If you want the 1-mana return spells anyway, you'd have to cut cascade. Then you'd be suspending Living End for 3 turns, and it stops being Living End.

results.prompt: Build a Pauper deck around Kiln Fiend.
results.text:
I built a Kiln Fiend version of Mono-Red Madness. Madness is the top deck in Pauper right now: Tier A, 17.6% of the field over the last 30 days. Kiln Fiend shows up in 26 lists across the format. In this deck it's fringe: 4 of 261 Madness lists run it, about 3.3 copies each. So it's a real variant, not a winning list.

**How I built it**
- I started from iamyep's 9-0 list that won Pauper Challenge 32 on 2026-10-07.
- I swapped out the 4 Voldaren Epicure for 4 Kiln Fiend. Epicure is in 77% of Madness lists. The 9-0 list ran it, but MisterTwin's two Challenge-winning lists didn't, so the slot is open.
- The rest of the main deck is standard. Lightning Bolt and Fiery Temper are in 100% of lists. Faithless Looting, Grab the Prize and Highway Robbery are each above 98%.

**Why Kiln Fiend fits**
- 35 of the 60 cards are instants or sorceries. Each one gives Kiln Fiend +3/+0 until end of turn.
- Lava Dart counts twice. Casting it is one spell, and casting it again from the graveyard is another, so that's +6/+0 for 1 mana and a sacrificed Mountain.
- Fiery Temper and Fireblast can be cast without paying their mana cost (Fiery Temper by discarding it, Fireblast by sacrificing two Mountains). Each still triggers the Fiend.
- The weakness: it's a 2-mana creature with 2 toughness that does nothing on its own. It dies to the cheap removal that Epicure's Blood tokens helped you play around.

**Sneaky Snacker**
Sneaky Snacker costs blue and black mana, but you almost never cast it. You discard it to Faithless Looting or Grab the Prize. It comes back from your graveyard when you draw your third card in a turn. The winning lists play 4 with 18 Mountains.

**Sideboard**
This is the usual Madness sideboard: Pyroblast (88% of lists), Relic of Progenitus (78%), Smash to Smithereens (78%), Red Elemental Blast (57%), End the Festivities (55%) and Searing Blaze (46%). It's not tuned for any one opponent. Name a matchup and I'll check that deck and score the sideboard against it.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue Premodern Dream Halls deck that wins with creatures instead of Brain Freeze. It passed the server's legality check, and the server labels it a brew. I didn't test it against specific opponents.

**What the field plays:** Dream Halls is a small deck right now. It has 0.8% meta share, 4 appearances and 1 League trophy in the last 30 days. Brain Freeze is in all 5 recorded lists, averaging 1.8 copies. So every recorded version wins with storm. I started from bparis15's mono-blue list from Premodern Challenge 16 on 2026-10-13, which went 2-3.

**What changed in the main deck:**
- **Out:** 3 Brain Freeze, 2 Flash of Insight, 1 Deep Analysis.
- **In:** 2 Palinchron, 2 Morphling, 2 Tidal Kraken.

**How it wins:**
- Dream Halls lets you discard a blue card instead of paying mana, so every creature here can come down for free. Show and Tell also puts them in play.
- **Tidal Kraken** is a 6/6 that can't be blocked, so it wins in about four attacks. It has not shown up in any recent results.
- **Palinchron** is a 4/5 flier that untaps seven lands when it enters. With Ancient Tomb and City of Traitors, that's enough mana to hard-cast Opportunity or a Kraken in the same turn. It appears in 151 recent Premodern lists.
- **Morphling** is cheaper and protects itself. Its ability to gain shroud stops removal like Swords to Plowshares. It appears in 84 recent lists.
- Intuition can find a creature or Dream Halls. If you have a creature in play, Rush of Knowledge draws cards equal to its mana cost. That's 8 off a Kraken and 7 off a Palinchron.

**The rest is stock:** All of these are in 100% of recorded lists: 4 Dream Halls, 4 Meditate, 4 Opportunity, 4 Ancient Tomb, Intuition, Frantic Search, Rush of Knowledge, City of Traitors, Svyelunite Temple and Arcane Denial.

**Sideboard:** Mostly bparis15's board.
- 2 Blue Elemental Blast and 2 Hydroblast for red decks like Sligh and Goblins. Blue Elemental Blast is in 100% of Dream Halls sideboards.
- I swapped Brain Freeze for 1 Stroke of Genius so there's no storm card anywhere. It can also make the opponent draw out their deck as a backup win.
- I swapped the extra Island for 1 Flash of Insight.

**Risks:**
- Show and Tell lets the opponent put a permanent into play too. Enchantress and Stiflenought can drop something big off it. Against those decks, rely on Dream Halls first.
- Creatures are easier to answer than Brain Freeze. Keep Arcane Denial and Chain of Vapor up to protect the creature you play.
- No one in the results has played this creature version, so expect to tune it.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
I built a brew: Eldrazi Tron with Peter Parker's Camera. The list passed the legality check.

**About the Camera**
- It's legal in Modern.
- It has not shown up in any results from the last 30 days, so this list is untested.
- The Camera costs 1. It enters with 3 film counters. Each time, you pay {2}, tap it and remove a counter to copy an activated or triggered ability you control.

**Why Eldrazi Tron**
- It's an A-tier deck with 4.2% of the field and 89 League trophies.
- Tron lands make the {2} cost easy to pay.
- Its strongest abilities are cast triggers and activated abilities, which is exactly what the Camera copies.

**What the Camera copies here**
- **Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger:** when you cast it, it exiles two permanents. A copy exiles two more.
- **Ugin, Eye of the Storms** (99% of Tron lists): copy the cast trigger to exile a second colored permanent. Ugin's 0 ability adds {C}{C}{C}, which pays for a Camera activation.
- **Devourer of Destiny** (99%): copy the cast trigger to exile a second colored permanent.
- **Sowing Mycospawn** (67%): a copy of the cast trigger puts a second land onto the battlefield. If you paid the kicker, you can also copy the trigger that exiles a land.
- **Expedition Map** (100%): one activation, copied, finds two lands. That gets you closer to all three Tron lands.
- **Karn, the Great Creator** (99%): copy the −2 to get two artifacts from your sideboard or exile. Karn can also fetch the Camera itself.

**Changes from the stock list**
- I started from kthanakit26's 8-1 list that won Modern Challenge 32 on 2026-10-14.
- Added 3 Camera to the main deck.
- Cut both main-deck Trinisphere (75% adoption). It taxes our own 1-mana artifacts, including Map, Boulder and the Camera.
- Cut 1 Giant's Boulder.

**Sideboard**
- This is the average Tron sideboard, with Vexing Bauble swapped for a fourth Camera that Karn can fetch.
- 1 Trinisphere stays for matchups where the tax helps you more than it hurts.
- Torpor Orb doesn't stop any of the Camera's targets. It only stops triggers from creatures entering the battlefield, and these are all cast triggers.

**Not included:** Emrakul, the Aeons Torn would give two extra turns with a copied cast trigger. It costs 15, and only 12% of Tron lists play it. If you want the big finish, swap it in for an Ulamog.

results.text:
I went with Hermit Druid Combo. It's the oddest deck in the Premodern field that still wins. It's a C-tier deck with 3.4% of the meta from 16 appearances, but it has 26 League trophies. That's more trophies than appearances, a better ratio than Enchantress (31 from 65) or Stiflenought (18 from 62). The list passed validation.

**Why it's weird**
- It plays no basic lands. All 22 lands are nonbasic: City of Brass, Gemstone Mine, the painlands, Reflecting Pool and the rest.
- Hermit Druid (in 100% of lists) mills your whole library, because it reveals cards until it finds a basic land and there are none.
- After the mill, Krosan Reclamation (100%) puts two cards back from your graveyard. It's in the 60 so you don't deck yourself.
- Unearth (3.4 copies on average), Shallow Grave, Animate Dead and Karmic Guide bring creatures back from the graveyard. Volrath's Shapeshifter copies whatever creature is on top of your graveyard.
- The finishers are one copy each of Palinchron, Phyrexian Devourer, Triskelion, Psychatog and Akroma.
- Survival of the Fittest (4 copies, 88%) is the second engine. It tutors creatures, and Squee and Battlefield Scrounger keep it running.
- Cabal Therapy (3.6 copies, 100%) checks the opponent's hand before you go off.

**The list**
- The 60 copies vcT's 5-0 League list card for card. The same list went 5-0 on 2026-10-12 and again on 2026-10-13.
- The sideboard is the field's usual board for this deck. Xantid Swarm (88%) protects the combo turn from counterspells. Pyroclasm (81%) answers creature decks like Sligh and Goblins. Naturalize (79%) handles hate enchantments and artifacts. Duress (79%) strips counterspells and other spells before you go off.

**Weak points**
- Graveyard hate wrecks this deck. Bring in Naturalize, Ray of Revelation and Uktabi Orangutan if the opponent shows artifact or enchantment hate.
- The mana base costs a lot of life against Sligh, which has 10.6% of the meta.

If you name the matchups you expect, I'll check each opponent and plan the sideboard card by card.
